title: pronto, veo, going to + vernos, la semana que viene, nos vemos

cards.title: Future context words
cards.body: With a future word, the present tense talks about the future: mañana, más tarde, esta noche, and pronto (soon, as in English 'get here pronto').

cards.title: ver: veo, ve, ven, ves, vemos
cards.body: The I form is slightly irregular: veo (vo would be too short).

cards.title: No guessing: rebuild from the 'to' form
cards.body: Ver → vemos (not 'venemos'). Keep 'who sees' and 'who is seen' as separate thoughts.

examples.en: Why aren't you seeing them soon?

cards.title: Going to + verb
cards.body: Without a future word, use ir a + verb, as in English. Work backwards from vamos to get vas.

examples.en: Are you going to see him soon?

cards.title: nos with going to
cards.body: Nos can go on the end of ver or before the changed verb.

examples.en: Are you going to see us soon?
examples.es: ¿Vas a vernos pronto? / ¿Nos vas a ver pronto?

examples.en: Why aren't you going to see us soon?
examples.es: ¿Por qué no vas a vernos pronto?

cards.title: la semana que viene = next week
cards.body: Literally 'the week that comes'. The we form also works as 'let's'.

cards.title: Strengthen the process, not the word
cards.body: Forgetting is fine: finding the word again (venir → vene → viene) strengthens the process. Build the sentence in the smallest pieces, one at a time, rather than translating the whole sentence at once.

cards.title: nos vemos = see you
cards.body: Nos means us, ourselves or each other. Nos vemos ('we see each other') is a common goodbye; saying goodbye is the future context.

examples.es: Nos vemos la semana que viene.

practice.why: la before veo; más tarde = later.

practice.en: Why aren't you (informal) seeing them (females) soon?
es: Por qué no las ves pronto

practice.en: Are you (informal) going to see him soon?
Are you (informal) going to see us soon?

es: Nos vemos la semana que viene
practice.why: nos vemos + la semana que viene.
